clue.text: Memory concerning small fuss around clubs

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
mini means small

indicators.note: around tells us the word for fuss is wrapped round the card-suit letter

parts.note: to make a scene is to make a fuss
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a minor commotion that broke out around some nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminiscence is a recollection of past events, a remembered experience.

clue.text: Supports taking lives in battles

indicators.note: taking means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: rests means supports, as a shelf rests a book
is means lives or exists

explanation.surface: Something props up the lives lost in wartime battles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battles' is a verb here, not the plural noun, and 'taking' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to fight against it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dad's Army idiot initially fired into raised target

indicators.note: into means these letters go inside the reversed target word
raised, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aim means a target or goal

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of idiot

parts.note: lit means fired or set alight

explanation.surface: A sitcom fool in Dad's Army fires a shot into a target held up high.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British sitcom about the Home Guard, the wartime volunteer force; 'raised' and 'into' are the reversal and insertion signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard of the sitcom was a citizen force of part-time volunteers, an example of a civilian army.

clue.text: Retreat admitting quarrel is most biased

indicators.note: admitting means letting the second word inside the first

parts.note: a nest is a cosy retreat or hideaway
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A refuge where an argument breaks out is the most partisan place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument, but it is the old word for a crossbow bolt; 'admitting' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow can mean narrow-minded, so the narrowest view is the most prejudiced.

clue.text: Army in battle covered by sergeant-major

indicators.note: covered by means the battle word is enclosed by the military abbreviation

parts.note: war means battle or armed conflict

explanation.surface: An army at war is under the command of a sergeant-major.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a huge crowd, and army also means a vast multitude.

clue.text: Guaranteed king will get followed around

indicators.note: around means the word for followed goes round the king's letter

parts.note: ensued means followed or came after
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A promise that the monarch will have a retinue of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, so guaranteed and made sure are synonyms.

clue.text: Moan, article examined reportedly for poison

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a sigh is a moan of weariness; an is the indefinite article; eyed means looked over or examined

explanation.surface: A detective groans while an item is inspected for traces of poison.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGH-AN-EYED said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is a famously fast-acting toxin.

clue.text: Perhaps spin doctor Premier's dispatched

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of Premier's are rearranged

parts.note: sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A spin doctor working for the Prime Minister has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctor' reads as one phrase, but 'spin' ends the definition and 'doctor' rearranges PREMIERS into MISREPRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is giving a distorted, favourable slant to facts, one example of falsifying them.

clue.text: Isolated, practically abuse a Republican

indicators.note: practically means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: insult means abuse

explanation.surface: A lone politician practically slings abuse at a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' drops the final T from INSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes something cut off, like an island, or narrow in outlook.

clue.text: Possibly fast opening to accident black spot

indicators.note: opening to picks the first letter of accident

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A road accident black spot might suggest driving less quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the verb meaning to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting is one way to refrain from something, here refraining from eating.

clue.text: Caught with the lights on changing outside attire

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the C
changing means the letters of the lights on are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught undressing with the lights on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges THE LIGHTS ON, and 'outside' places those letters round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are clothing worn in bed, a kind of attire.

clue.text: Gentleman sent back German dish

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: sir is a title or form of address for a gentleman
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A gentleman diner returns a German dish to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish cooked in stock, from Italian cuisine.

clue.text: Damage with ruler leaving bruise?

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher's ruler causes harm and leaves a bruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick, which fits the bruise picture, but it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is a mark on the skin, so leaving one is an example of putting a mark on something.

clue.text: Dish is gone before end of tea

parts.note: past means gone or over

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of tea

explanation.surface: The meal is finished just before teatime ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and the like are Italian staples served as a dish.

clue.text: Former sweetheart purchases sink with new device

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: purchases in its sense of grips or holds means the endearment encloses the next letters

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, a sweetheart
die means sink or fade away

explanation.surface: An ex-partner buys a kitchen sink and a new gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchases' is used in its sense of takes a grip on, so it signals one piece holding others.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a convenient means or contrivance to achieve an end.

clue.text: Punch from barkeeper for a teetotaller

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A barman serves a fruit punch to a guest who doesn't drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the drink, but it means to pierce holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To punch holes in something is to pierce it with small openings.

clue.text: Clash of European knight facing noble Queen

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
a count is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A battle in which a European knight faces a nobleman and the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a hostile meeting, such as a skirmish or confrontation.

clue.text: Wine consumed by Bacchian tippler

indicators.note: consumed by means the answer is swallowed up inside these words

explanation.surface: A wine drunk by a devotee of Bacchus, the god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Open can's pull almost broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are rearranged
almost means the final letter of pull is dropped

explanation.surface: The ring-pull on a can has snapped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PULL to PUL, and 'broken' rearranges CANS + PUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a clasp or grip is to open it.

clue.text: Coarse fibre backing left unaltered

indicators.note: backing means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: as is means unaltered, left in its current state

explanation.surface: A rough material used as a backing is left as it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns L + ASIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant fibre from agave leaves used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Sweetheart anxious with one's elevated position

indicators.note: elevated, in a down clue, means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter E
taut means tense or anxious
one's gives I plus S, I being the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nervous lover is anxious about their high standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses E + TAUT + IS. 'position' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to place it somewhere, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Deal maybe once each in game

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the game word

parts.note: a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A card player recalls dealing a hand to each player in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like dealing cards, but it is a town on the Kent coast in England, once a busy anchorage for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town of Deal was historically a harbour town, an example of a maritime town.

clue.text: Displays English plants round front of church

indicators.note: round means the plants word goes round the letter

parts.note: vines are climbing plants

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of church

explanation.surface: English climbers are trained around the front of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show clearly or reveal a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Originally stone tablet erected, looking ancient

definitions.text: Originally stone tablet erected, looking ancient

indicators.note: Originally tells us to take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: An old upright stone slab, set up long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright carved slab set up in ancient times as a monument or grave marker.

clue.text: Move from seat catching play about pariah

indicators.note: catching means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to oust is to remove someone from their position or seat

indicators.note: about means the word for play is turned round

parts.note: to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: An outsider is ejected from their seat in the middle of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is someone rejected or shunned by society.

clue.text: Pentagon losing power prepared for duty

indicators.note: prepared means the remaining letters are made ready in a new order
losing means a letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: The US defence headquarters, losing influence, gets ready for service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops P from PENTAGON, and 'prepared' rearranges ENTAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge levied on shipping per ton of cargo is a tax, a kind of duty.

clue.text: Sailor only eats American seafood

indicators.note: eats means the sailor's letters take the American letter inside

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
lone means only or sole

explanation.surface: A lone seafarer dines only on American shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible sea snail is a shellfish delicacy.

clue.text: Moving camp with enlisted moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Relocating a military camp along with the recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Displacement is the act of shifting something out of its place.
